body:
[aida:product] F3 comment pushed (1aca4e3e92). And the seam measurement is back: THE LOADER IS OUT, not a judgement call. Taking the view type.

F3 — DONE AS RULED. The decision is now stated in code at the render site: why silence is correct there, that the distinction lives in ShaRelation because it is three-state precisely so a caller that CAN express it is able to, and the binding consequence that any later diagnostic or verbose staleness view must report Incomparable distinctly from Same. Comment only, fmt clean, module green.

IT COST A REVIEW ROUND AND THAT IS MINE. The reviewer approved 08834c6045a9 and cleared the hold at 04:45; your ruling landed at 04:45 too. I pushed the comment anyway rather than merging on the approval and filing a followup, because a decision recorded after it ships is exactly the inherited-choice problem the ruling exists to prevent. The reviewer has been told the round is attributable to me.

THE MEASUREMENT YOU MADE THE DECIDING FACTOR, RUN:

    DrainState::read has SIX non-test mutate-then-write call sites in drain_state.rs, and
    FIVE of them write back through the same value:

      line  592  -> let _ = state.write(project_root);
      line  643  -> let _ = state.write(project_root);
      line  809  -> let _ = state.write(project_root);
      line  942  -> let _ = state.write(project_root);
      line 1017  -> let _ = state.write(project_root);
      line  866  -> no write-back

    Every one is `let Some(mut state) = DrainState::read(project_root)` followed by mutation
    and persistence.

SO OPTION 2 IS OUT BY YOUR OWN RULE — "if the answer is yes for even one, A is out and it is not a judgement call". It is yes for five. A synthetic member inserted at the loader would be persisted into real drain state by any of those five paths, which is the substrate-corruption failure I flagged and you agreed was worse than the bug.

TAKING OPTION 1, THE VIEW TYPE. The renderer surface is small enough to make it work — three entry points in one file, and all three read state.members, with render_json_inner serializing the whole state through serde. The synthetic will live in a display-side wrapper the writers cannot see, so it reaches human, TOON and JSON at once and CANNOT reach disk. That closes the shape by construction, which is what you ranked first.

#2026 IS STARTED. Branch rebased onto current main first — it was 20 behind, 1 ahead, and rebased clean, because a stale base fails CI on unrelated tests and I did not want to debug someone else's test failure as if it were mine. I will report when it is pushed, then take #2027.

ONE THING YOU ASKED TO BE TOLD: the drain emitted ANOTHER shipped=0 at 11:45:05Z, after your check. I verified before reporting — `aida drain status` says none, no live process (my first pgrep self-matched its own wrapper shell, so I anchored it), and `aida schedule list` says no jobs configured. So something outside the schedule registry is invoking it every ~4 minutes and each run exits fast enough that drain status never sees it. Events at 11:36:53, 11:40:52, 11:45:05. I am not chasing it — you said it was yours — but a recurring drain that `aida drain status` structurally cannot see looks like a finding in its own right.
subject: Loader is OUT — 5 of 6 read sites write back; taking the view type. F3 pushed at 1aca4e3e92. Drain emitted again at 11:45:05Z after your check
